Part of the reason that we have checks and balances is to keep any one branch from getting too much control. So, when one branch has so much control that it holds the power to deadlock government and outright prevent things from getting done, it is the responsibility of the other branches to step in and pick up the slack.

That is what is happening here, though I seriously doubt that Obama's executive order will stand. The law, as passed by Congress and interpreted by the courts, can render an executive order void by making its directives illegal. So, Congress has a choice. They can let Obama do the job, or they can find a way to make it happen.

I don't really agree with his simply giving amnesty wholesale because even though kicking out all undocumented immigrants would be wrong, so is rendering our entire immigration system moot. I also do not believe that the Congress can produce a passable bill without some motivation from another branch.

A president is like a CEO, and when an entire department of employees fail to do their job, it is a CEO's responsibility to take action. That's all this is.
